source: RBI Banks in India page plus primary sources per bank (see evidenceUrls)

banks.name: State Bank of India

history.event: Bank of Calcutta established; chartered as Bank of Bengal on 2 Jan 1809
Bank of Bombay incorporated
Bank of Madras incorporated
Bank of Bengal, Bank of Bombay and Bank of Madras amalgamated into the Imperial Bank of India
State Bank of India Act, 1955 (Act 23 of 1955, enacted 8 May 1955) came into force; Imperial Bank of India's undertaking transferred to newly constituted State Bank of India
State Bank of India (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959 (Act 38 of 1959) enacted, enabling SBI to take over 8 former state-associated banks as subsidiaries (later called Associates)
State Bank of Bikaner & Jaipur, State Bank of Hyderabad, State Bank of Mysore, State Bank of Patiala, State Bank of Travancore and Bharatiya Mahila Bank merged into SBI

banks.notes: Full lineage traced 1806-1955-2017. Founding date used (1955-07-01) is the constitution of SBI itself; the bank's own material traces continuous heritage to 1806 via predecessor Presidency Banks / Imperial Bank of India (see history array and Imperial Bank of India predecessor entry).

Nationalised (one of 14 banks); 'The Bank of Baroda Ltd.' became 'Bank of Baroda'
Benares State Bank amalgamated (RBI-directed rescue)
Dena Bank and Vijaya Bank amalgamated into Bank of Baroda (mega-merger)

banks.name: Bank of India

Nationalised (one of 14 banks)

predecessors.name: Bank of Calcutta / Bank of Bengal
predecessors.notes: Bank of Calcutta founded 2 Jun 1806; rechartered as Bank of Bengal 2 Jan 1809. One of 3 Presidency Banks amalgamated into Imperial Bank of India 27 Jan 1921, which in turn became SBI 1 Jul 1955.

predecessors.name: Bank of Bombay
predecessors.notes: Presidency Bank; amalgamated into Imperial Bank of India 1921.

predecessors.name: Bank of Madras
predecessors.notes: Presidency Bank; amalgamated into Imperial Bank of India 1921.

predecessors.name: Imperial Bank of India
predecessors.notes: Formed 1921 from amalgamation of the 3 Presidency Banks; became State Bank of India 1 Jul 1955 under the SBI Act, 1955.

predecessors.name: State Bank of Bikaner & Jaipur
predecessors.notes: Formed 1 Jan 1963 by merger of Bank of Bikaner (est. 1944 by Maharaja Ganga Singh) and Bank of Jaipur (est. 1943); both became SBI subsidiaries in 1960. Merged into SBI 1 Apr 2017 (Gazette notification 22 Feb 2017).

predecessors.name: State Bank of Hyderabad
predecessors.notes: Founded as Hyderabad State Bank by the 7th Nizam, Mir Osman Ali Khan, under the Hyderabad State Bank Act, 1941 (first branch opened 5 Apr 1942). Renamed State Bank of Hyderabad 1956 when RBI took it over as first subsidiary; became SBI subsidiary 1 Oct 1959. Merged into SBI 1 Apr 2017 (RBI press release prid=39884 confirms merger date; founding history is secondary/Wikipedia, corroborated by contemporary press e.g. Hindu Business Line and Gulf News/IANS).

predecessors.name: State Bank of Mysore
predecessors.notes: Established as 'The Bank of Mysore Ltd' 19 May 1913 (commenced business 2 Oct 1913) under patronage of Maharaja Krishna Raja Wadiyar IV, at the instance of Sir M. Visvesvaraya. Became SBI subsidiary 10 Sep 1959 (per Wikipedia; a secondary source gives 1 Mar 1960). Merged into SBI 1 Apr 2017.

predecessors.name: State Bank of Patiala
predecessors.notes: Founded as Patiala State Bank by Maharaja Bhupinder Singh, 17 Nov 1917. Reorganised as 'Bank of Patiala' 1948 (PEPSU formation); absorbed Bank of Faridkot and Jind Cooperative Bank 1949. Became SBI subsidiary 1 Apr 1960, renamed State Bank of Patiala, absorbed Kalsia State Bank same month. Merged into SBI 1 Apr 2017.

predecessors.name: State Bank of Travancore
predecessors.notes: Established 1945 as Travancore Bank Ltd at the initiative of Diwan C.P. Ramaswami Iyer. Became SBI subsidiary 1960 under the SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act 1959, renamed State Bank of Travancore. Merged into SBI 1 Apr 2017.

predecessors.name: Bharatiya Mahila Bank
predecessors.notes: India's first bank exclusively for women; inaugurated 19 Nov 2013 by PM Manmohan Singh, announced in the Feb 2013 Union Budget. Merged into SBI 1 Apr 2017 per Gazette notification dated 20 Mar 2017 under Section 35(2) of the SBI Act, 1955.

predecessors.name: State Bank of Saurashtra
predecessors.notes: Formed 1950 under the Saurashtra State Banks (Amalgamation) Ordinance, 1950 from Bhavnagar Darbar Bank (est. 1902) plus 4 smaller Darbar banks (Rajkot, Porbandar, Palitana, Vadia), merged with effect from 1 Jul 1950. Became an SBI subsidiary in 1960 under the SBI (Subsidiary Banks) Act, 1959. Merged into SBI effective 13 Aug 2008 per Gazette notification dated 13 Aug 2008 (Acquisition of State Bank of Saurashtra Order, 2008).

predecessors.name: State Bank of Indore
predecessors.notes: Founding year not independently verified in this pass (a secondary blog gives 1920 as 'Bank of Indore'); set to null per standards. Merged into SBI with effect from close of business 26 Aug 2010 (Gazette notification dated 28 Jul 2010, 'Acquisition of State Bank of Indore Order, 2010'; SBI's own Sep-2010 results notes confirm 26 Aug 2010 as effective date).

predecessors.name: Benares State Bank
predecessors.notes: Established 1946 (Wikipedia/Bank of Baroda's own history page says BSB 'traced its origins back to 1871' as treasury office of Benares state, formally established as a bank 1946). Acquired Bareilly Bank (1964) and Lucknow Bank (1968). Amalgamated with Bank of Baroda per Government notification; PTI wire report (dated 20 Jun 2002, a Thursday) states the Union government approved the amalgamation and that it 'comes into effect from today'. Exact Gazette effective date not independently re-confirmed from the Gazette text itself in this pass -- treat the day-level date as moderately confident, not primary-certain.

predecessors.name: Dena Bank
predecessors.notes: Founded 26 May 1938 as Devkaran Nanjee Banking Company by sons of Devkaran Nanjee; renamed Dena Bank Dec 1939. Nationalised 19 Jul 1969 (Dena Bank's own BSE-filed prospectus confirms 'constituted under the Banking Companies Act, 1970 on July 19, 1969'). Merged into Bank of Baroda 1 Apr 2019 together with Vijaya Bank.

predecessors.name: Vijaya Bank
predecessors.notes: Established 23 Oct 1931 (Vijayadashami day) in Mangalore by A.B. Shetty and 14 Bunt community members. Nationalised 15 Apr 1980 (one of 6 banks). Merged into Bank of Baroda 1 Apr 2019 together with Dena Bank.

predecessors.name: New Bank of India
predecessors.notes: Incorporated 21 Dec 1936 in Lahore as 'The New Bank Limited' by Mulk Raj Kohli; renamed 'The New Bank of India Limited' 4 Nov 1941 (per successor NBFC entity's own company-profile page, nbi-india.co.in). Nationalised 1980 (one of 6 banks). Amalgamated into PNB per the 'New Bank of India (Amalgamation and Transfer of Undertaking) Scheme, 1993', notified 4 Sep 1993 under Section 9 of the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Act, 1980.

predecessors.name: Nedungadi Bank
predecessors.notes: Oldest private-sector bank in Kerala (per Wikipedia/PNB); founding year not independently verified in this pass, set to null. Placed under RBI moratorium ~Nov 2002; amalgamated into PNB pursuant to the Scheme of Amalgamation notified by the Government of India on 31 Jan 2003 (per PNB's own official document). PNB physically took over branches on 1 Feb 2003 per contemporaneous PTI wire report. NOTE: the research brief's mention of a '2005' merger date for Nedungadi Bank does not match any primary source found; 31 Jan 2003 (PNB's own notification date) is used here.

predecessors.name: Oriental Bank of Commerce
predecessors.notes: Founded 19 Feb 1943 in Lahore by Rai Bahadur Lala Sohan Lal; registered office shifted to India after Partition. Nationalised 15 Apr 1980 (confirmed via apraca.org bank profile PDF). Amalgamated into PNB 1 Apr 2020 together with United Bank of India (announced 30 Aug 2019, Cabinet approval 4 Mar 2020).

predecessors.name: United Bank of India
predecessors.notes: Formed by RBI-assisted amalgamation of 4 Bengal-based banks -- Comilla Banking Corporation (est. 1914), Bengal Central Bank (est. 1918, renamed United Bank of India Ltd), Comilla Union Bank (est. 1922) and Hooghly Bank (est. 1932) -- after all four suffered runs following the 1938 failure of Nath Bank. RBI sanctioned the scheme by order dated 18 Dec 1950, effective retroactively from 1 Jan 1950 (Calcutta High Court income-tax judgment citing the RBI order). Nationalised 19 Jul 1969. Amalgamated into PNB 1 Apr 2020 together with Oriental Bank of Commerce.

predecessors.name: Global Trust Bank
predecessors.notes: Founded 21 Oct 1994 at Secunderabad by Ramesh Gelli and others (Wikipedia; founding date not independently confirmed via a primary GTB source since the bank no longer exists). Placed under RBI Moratorium from close of business 24 Jul 2004; amalgamated into Oriental Bank of Commerce with effect from 14 Aug 2004 per Government of India-sanctioned Scheme (RBI press release, primary). OBC subsequently amalgamated into PNB 1 Apr 2020, so GTB's chain of succession is GTB -> OBC (2004) -> PNB (2020).

predecessors.name: Andhra Bank
predecessors.notes: Founded by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya; registered 20 Nov 1923, commenced business 28 Nov 1923 in Machilipatnam. Nationalised 15 Apr 1980 (one of 6 banks). Amalgamated into Union Bank of India 1 Apr 2020 together with Corporation Bank.

predecessors.name: Corporation Bank
predecessors.notes: Founded 12 Mar 1906 in Udupi as 'Canara Banking Corporation (Udipi) Ltd' by Khan Bahadur Haji Abdullah Haji Kasim Saheb Bahadur, with Rs 5,000 capital. Nationalised 15 Apr 1980. Amalgamated into Union Bank of India 1 Apr 2020 together with Andhra Bank.

predecessors.name: Syndicate Bank
predecessors.notes: Founded 20 Oct 1925 in Udupi as 'Canara Industrial and Banking Syndicate Limited' by T.M.A. Pai, Upendra Ananth Pai and Vaman Srinivas Kudva; renamed Syndicate Bank 1964, HQ shifted to Manipal. Nationalised 19 Jul 1969 (one of 14 banks). Amalgamated into Canara Bank 1 Apr 2020 (announced 30 Aug 2019).

predecessors.name: Allahabad Bank
predecessors.notes: Founded 24 Apr 1865 at Allahabad (Prayagraj) by a group of Europeans; oldest joint-stock bank in India (155 years) until its merger. Nationalised 19 Jul 1969 (one of 14 banks). Amalgamated into Indian Bank 1 Apr 2020 (announced 30 Aug 2019).

predecessors.name: Times Bank
predecessors.notes: RBI in-principle approval to Bennett, Coleman & Co (Times Group) Dec 1993; incorporated 6 Jul 1994, certificate of commencement of business 22 Aug 1994, banking licence Apr 1995, first branch (D.N. Road, Mumbai) opened 8 Jun 1995. Merged into HDFC Bank effective 26 Feb 2000 (HDFC Bank's own site confirms the merger date as primary; Times Bank's own founding/incorporation dates are corroborated by a detailed secondary account -- bankerstrust.in column by Tamal Bandyopadhyay -- rather than a surviving primary Times Bank source).

predecessors.name: Centurion Bank of Punjab
predecessors.notes: Formed 2005-06 from the merger of Centurion Bank (est. 1994) and Bank of Punjab (est. 1995); this predecessor lineage (Centurion Bank <-> Bank of Punjab formation) was not independently verified against a primary source in this pass and is therefore omitted from 'founded'/history, left as null -- flagged for follow-up. What is confirmed (primary, HDFC Bank's own site): Lord Krishna Bank merged into Centurion Bank of Punjab 29 Aug 2007, and HDFC Bank's acquisition/amalgamation of Centurion Bank of Punjab was approved by RBI 23 May 2008 for ₹9,510 crore, the then-largest such merger in Indian financial services.

predecessors.name: Lord Krishna Bank
predecessors.notes: Kerala-based old private bank; founding year not independently verified in this pass (set to null). RBI sanctioned the amalgamation of Lord Krishna Bank Ltd with Centurion Bank of Punjab under Section 44A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, effective 29 Aug 2007 (appointed date retroactive to 1 Apr 2006), following AGM approvals in Sep 2006 and dismissal of a shareholder challenge by the Kerala High Court. Chain: Lord Krishna Bank -> Centurion Bank of Punjab (2007) -> HDFC Bank (2008).

predecessors.name: HDFC Limited (Housing Development Finance Corporation Ltd)
predecessors.notes: India's largest housing finance company, founded 1977 by H.T. Parekh; also HDFC Bank's founding promoter/parent (1994). Merger with HDFC Bank announced 4 Apr 2022, NCLT-approved 17 Mar 2023, effective 1 Jul 2023 -- India's largest-ever M&A deal.

predecessors.name: Bank of Madura
predecessors.notes: Old private-sector bank based in Madurai, Tamil Nadu; founding year not independently verified in this pass (set to null). Merged into ICICI Bank effective 10 Mar 2001, share-exchange ratio 2 ICICI Bank shares for every 1 Bank of Madura share.

predecessors.name: The Sangli Bank
predecessors.notes: Founded 1916, headquartered in Sangli, Maharashtra; ~30% owned by the Bhate family; 198 branches (158 Maharashtra, 31 Karnataka) at time of merger. All-stock amalgamation approved by both banks' boards 9 Dec 2006, RBI approval effective 19 Apr 2007.

predecessors.name: Bank of Rajasthan
predecessors.notes: Established at Udaipur on 8 May 1943 (Akshaya Tritiya) with initial capital Rs 10 lakh; founder chairman Seth Govind Ram Seksaria; promoted by the Mansingka brothers of Bhilwara at the urging of Mewar finance minister Rai Bahadur P.C. Chatterji. The state of Rajasthan is said to be named partly after this bank. Amalgamated into ICICI Bank with effect from close of business 12 Aug 2010 (announced May 2010, share-swap 25 ICICI Bank shares for every 118 Bank of Rajasthan shares). Evidence sourced from the Wayback Machine capture (Dec 2010) of the bank's own website, taken shortly after the merger -- treated as primary/first-party content.

predecessors.name: UTI Bank (pre-rename identity of Axis Bank)
predecessors.notes: Not a merger of two distinct banks -- this is a corporate rename of the same legal entity ('UTI Bank Ltd' to 'Axis Bank Ltd', effective 30 Jul 2007 per RBI Second Schedule notification). Included here only to make the lineage/rename explicit for the tracker; mergedOn reflects the rename date, not an amalgamation date.

predecessors.name: ING Vysya Bank (Vysya Bank)
predecessors.notes: Vysya Bank incorporated 1930 in Bangalore, serving the Vysya trading community; RBI licence 1958. Dutch ING Group acquired an equity stake starting 1998-2002 (raised to 44% in 2002); renamed ING Vysya Bank 2003. Merged into Kotak Mahindra Bank effective 1 Apr 2015 (announced 20 Nov 2014, RBI-approved 1 Apr 2015, integration completed 15 May 2016) -- the first merger of an Indian bank with a foreign-owned bank's Indian arm structured this way.

predecessors.name: United Western Bank
predecessors.notes: Founded 1936 in Satara, Maharashtra by Annasaheb Chirmule (who earlier founded Satara Swadeshi Commercial Bank in 1907); incorporated 1936, commenced operations 8 Mar 1937. Became a Scheduled Bank 1951; acquired Union Bank of Kolhapur (1956) and Satara Swadeshi Commercial Bank (1961). Placed under RBI moratorium 2 Sep 2006 after losses eroded capital; amalgamated into IDBI Ltd (now IDBI Bank) with effect from 3 Oct 2006 under Section 45 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 -- confirmed via IDBI Bank's own official history document.

predecessors.name: Fincare Small Finance Bank
predecessors.notes: Founding year not independently verified in this pass (set to null); Fincare SFB began as a microfinance-origin Small Finance Bank licensed in the 2017 SFB cohort. Scheme of Amalgamation of Fincare SFB into AU SFB became effective 1 Apr 2024; Fincare shareholders received 579 AU SFB shares for every 2,000 Fincare SFB shares held.

predecessors.name: Capital Local Area Bank Limited (pre-conversion identity of Capital SFB)
predecessors.notes: Not a merger of two distinct banks -- this is the same legal entity converting from a Local Area Bank licence to a Small Finance Bank licence (renamed 15 Apr 2016, commenced SFB business 24 Apr 2016, per RBI's own press release the Local Area Bank licence was surrendered/ceased on that date). Included for lineage clarity per the research brief.

predecessors.name: Shivalik Mercantile Co-operative Bank Limited (pre-conversion identity of Shivalik SFB)
predecessors.notes: Not a merger of two distinct banks -- an Urban Co-operative Bank voluntarily transitioning to a Small Finance Bank under RBI's Sep-2018 transition scheme; the co-operative banking licence was cancelled on transition (RBI press release prid=52624, dated 26 Nov 2021, confirms cancellation 'upon its transition' with the SFB licence dated 1 Jan 2021 and operations from 26 Apr 2021). Included for lineage clarity.

predecessors.name: North East Small Finance Bank Limited (pre-rename identity of slice SFB)
predecessors.notes: Not a merger of two distinct banks -- the slice fintech group (Garagepreneurs Internet, Quadrillion Finance, Intergalactory Foundry) merged INTO North East SFB on 27 Oct 2024, after which the combined entity (retaining NESFB's banking licence) was renamed 'slice Small Finance Bank Limited' effective per RBI notification dated 14 May 2025. See slice-sfb current-bank entry for full lineage/history array.

predecessors.name: Punjab and Maharashtra Co-operative Bank (PMC Bank)
predecessors.notes: Multi-state urban co-operative bank; founding year not independently verified in this pass (set to null). RBI superseded PMC Bank's board and imposed withdrawal restrictions Sep 2019 after HDIL-linked financial irregularities were discovered. Amalgamated into Unity Small Finance Bank under a Government of India-notified Scheme with effect from 25 Jan 2022; upheld against a depositor legal challenge by the Bombay High Court in Mar 2026 per Wikipedia.

notes: Compiled 2026-09-27 by web research (RBI press releases/notifications/history pages, bank official 'About us'/'History' pages, Gazette-derived primary-law texts via indiacode.nic.in/advocatekhoj/indiankanoon, and corroborating secondary press) using ExaSearch/ExaContents and curl against rbi.org.in. Standards followed: no invented values (unverifiable fields are null with a note in the entry); Wikipedia used only as a lead and, where flagged sourceType/notes say so, as the operative secondary source when no primary source could be retrieved (mostly for pre-independence founder/founding-day detail on defunct predecessor banks). Two explicit corrections vs. the research brief's assumptions: (1) Nedungadi Bank's amalgamation into PNB is dated 31 Jan 2003 by PNB's own published notice, not 2005; (2) Central Bank of India's founding is dated 21 Dec 1911 (bank's own site, 2011 Presidential centenary speech, current Wikipedia infobox) rather than the 11 Dec 1911 date given in one secondary biography. Not attempted/left for follow-up: exhaustive verification of every SFB/payments-bank MFI-to-SFB predecessor beyond the ones named in the brief; Centurion Bank of Punjab's own pre-2005 formation (Centurion Bank + Bank of Punjab) founding dates; a handful of exact day-level founding dates for banks whose own current websites give only a year (CSB Bank, Dhanlaxmi Bank, DCB Bank, Nedungadi Bank, Bank of Madura, Lord Krishna Bank, PMC Bank, State Bank of Indore, Fincare SFB, Centurion Bank of Punjab -- all left null rather than guessed).
